text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — continuous-batch latency cliff and KV cache blowout detected in us-east-1. Alerts: cb_queue_depth > 1000, kv_eviction_rate 98%, p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 1.8s. Auto-scaler kicking, some requests 5xx. Pager: @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: on it. acked. grabbing runbook and perf dashboards. linking main graphs: https://dash/redwood/cb?range=15m
maya_prodeng: looking now — cb-runtime nodes show continuous batching queue depth spike starting 1839998600. pattern looks like a prefetch feedback loop: many concurrent requests causing large prefetched prefixes that expand microbatch sizes -> KV miss storm -> full-cache evictions.

jon_dev: hmm. any recent deploys or config rollouts?
mike_oncall: no code deploys in last hour. config flags: batching.max_tokens=512, prefetch.concurrency=32.
maya_prodeng: those defaults might be fine at low qps but at high concurrency they blow out. I'm seeing microbatch sizes jump to ~400 tokens and kv caching eviction churn.

priya_sre: customer-impact: big-retailer-prod and acme-labs have elevated 5xx rates (~35% of requests) and some streaming responses timing out. CS is paged.
sam_support: I'll open a bridge for CS updates. templating note: "We're actively investigating performance issue affecting streaming and some inference requests"

mike_oncall: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce prefetch.concurrency from 32 -> 4 2) lower batching.max_tokens 512 -> 128 3) enable immediate microbatch cap to 64 tokens per request 4) temporarily route heavy traffic to fallback model (lower mem footprint).
maya_prodeng: agree. let's do (1) and (2) first — should reduce KV pressure and microbatch explosion quickly. I'll prepare a hotfix rollout to canary.

jon_dev: commands:
```
# reduce prefetch concurrency via k/v config
kubectl -n prod patch configmap cb-runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/prefetch.concurrency","value":"4"}]'
# reduce max tokens
kubectl -n prod patch configmap cb-runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/batching.max_tokens","value":"128"}]'
```

mike_oncall: applying patch to one canary node now. will watch metrics and logs.
deploy-bot: deploy started: cb-config-hotfix-183999 on canary pool (1/3).
maya_prodeng: logs from canary show queue depth dropping within 30s, kv_eviction_rate back down to 20%. p95 latency trending down.
mike_oncall: rolling to remaining nodes.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: cb-config-hotfix-183999 rolled to 12 nodes.

priya_sre: monitoring SLOs — big-retailer error rate falling from 35% -> 8% in last 5m, acme-labs similar. customer-impact update: partial degradation during 1839998600-1839998900 window, now degraded but recovering. recommending incident severity remain P1 until full recovery confirmed.
sam_support: sending PSAT to affected customers and a brief timeline.

maya_prodeng: next step: reduce per-request microbatch cap (hotpatch) to avoid future oscillation and add an autoscaling knob for prefetch rate. I'll file a follow-up PR.

jon_dev: proposed microbatch cap change (hotpatch):
```
# runtime flag
--microbatch.max_tokens=64
```
mike_oncall: I'm going to stage that as a canary hotpatch. will notify when live.

mike_oncall: canary hotpatch applied at 1839999250. observing for 5m.
maya_prodeng: metrics look good — microbatch distribution now peaks at 60 tokens, no secondary eviction spike.

priya_sre: CS: sent update to big-retailer and acme-labs. they acknowledged and requested postmortem.
sam_support: created customer incident links and escalations doc: https://tickets/redwood/INC-10023

mike_oncall: preparing handoff. I'm going offline in ~30m, handing to @sam_support for follow-up and postmortem. Key actions for follow-up: - validate long-tail latency over next 2 hours - confirm no regression in low-qps workloads - coordinate PRs for config thresholds + guardrails - add alert for prefetch feedback loop (kv_eviction_rate spike)
sam_support: ack. will monitor and coordinate postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated (partial) — postmortem required. opened ticket PM-183999.

priya_sre: initial RCA (brief): emergent prefetch feedback loop at high concurrency causing microbatch size blowouts; KV cache couldn't sustain working set leading to mass evictions and latency cliff. Contributing factors: high prefetch.concurrency default, no microbatch hard cap, and missing alert for kv_eviction_rate spikes.
maya_prodeng: follow-ups: 1) enforce microbatch hard cap in runtime 2) autoscale prefetch based on kv occupancy 3) add canary test that ramps concurrency in staging 4) improve dashboards/alerts for kv churn

mike_oncall: thanks team. leaving detailed timeline and logs in the incident doc. handing off. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 1839999500. severity downgraded to P2 while follow-ups tracked.
